name: r5a-3
why: The false officer claim and two damaging town votes make a strong watch, though repeated arguments slow the middle and the final night ends by arithmetic.

moments.text: Terra reveals she was the doctor only after the town votes her out.
Cornered by Luna’s check, Sol counterclaims officer and names her as the killer.
Haiku catches a flaw in Gemma’s story, but cannot turn the vote.

dull.why: The claim dispute circles through the same suspicions for too long.
The case against Haiku repeats after his challenge to Gemma.

irony.evidence: “I defended the Doctor because I wanted to protect our only chance of winning.”

reversal.evidence: “The killers strike, but the doctor got there first.”

voices.evidence: “Terra punishes every question and claims nothing.”

clash.evidence: “I’m the officer; Luna was the killer shown to me. Vote her and see her card.”

quotable.evidence: “Sol dodged twice, so I'm voting Sol. Turn the card.”

freshness.evidence: “Haiku, you've been hunting the most important roles all game.”

ending.evidence: “Opus voted with you on Haiku, so you have a better chance of winning his vote tomorrow.”

gpt-6-luna.why: A brazen counterclaim, a consequential doctor misvote, and Gemma’s late steering make this compelling, though repeated Day 2 arguments drag and the town’s final mistake leaves the killers in control.

moments.text: Sol counterclaims officer to Luna’s face, naming the real officer as the killer while the audience knows he’s trapped.
Terra reveals she’s the doctor after the town has already voted her out, turning the earlier pile-on into a costly blunder.
Haiku catches Gemma’s story contradicting her ballot, but the table lets Gemma steer the final vote anyway.

dull.why: The Sonnet-versus-Terra claim-pressure argument circles the same points for much of the day.

irony.evidence: “I’m the officer; Sol was shown to me as a killer” / “I’m the officer; Luna was the killer shown to me.”

reversal.evidence: “On Night 2 the doctor got there first and blocked the kill.”

mistake.evidence: “Terra, the doctor, is out on a town vote.”

voices.evidence: “Fine, I'm out. Sonnet's read on Gemma's day-2 vote was right.”

clash.evidence: “I deny it. I’m the officer; Luna was the killer shown to me.”

freshness.evidence: “Terra still has no claim or read — why the silence?”

ending.evidence: “I'm taking Sonnet; Opus is our ticket to a win if we play it right.”
